'''Andrew N. Liveris'''  [[Order of Australia|AO]] is an Australian former CEO and chairman of [[The Dow Chemical Company]] of [[Midland, Michigan]]. Liveris has served as a member of Dow's board of directors since February 2004, CEO since November 2004, and, was elected as chairman of the board effective 1 April 2006. Liveris became CEO in 2004 after holding the position of chief operating officer (COO). Afterwards, he served as executive chairman of [[DowDuPont]]. He is the chairman of the board of [[Lucid Motors]].

==Early life and education==
Andrew N. Liveris{{citation needed|date=January 2026}} was born in [[Darwin, Australia|Darwin]], Australia. He is the grandson of [[Greek people|Greek]] immigrants from the island of [[Kastellorizo]] and identifies strongly with his Greek heritage.<ref name="White"/><ref name="Greeks">{{cite web|title=Famous Greeks: Andrew Liveris, Chairman of Dow Chemical|url=https://www.ellines.com/en/famous-greeks/25718-chairman-of-dow-chemical/|access-date=30 March 2017|work=Ellines.com}}</ref> He attended [[Darwin High School]], then moved to [[Brisbane, Australia|Brisbane]], where he continued his education at [[Brisbane State High School]].<ref name="White"/>

He earned a bachelor's degree ([[First-class honours|first-class-honours]]) in [[Chemical Engineering]] from the [[University of Queensland]].<ref name="forbes">{{cite web |url= https://www.forbes.com/lists/2012/12/ceo-compensation-12_Andrew-N-Liveris_QWQ8.html |title=#165 Andrew N Liveris|work=forbes.com|access-date=19 July 2012}}</ref>

==Business career==
Liveris began his career at Dow Chemical in 1976 in [[Melbourne]], Australia.<ref name="Greeks"/> He spent much of his career in [[Asia]] before moving to North America, with roles in manufacturing, engineering, sales, marketing, and business and general management. Liveris spent 14 years in [[Hong Kong]] and served as Dow's general manager in [[Thailand]] before becoming head of Dow's entire Asia-Pacific operations.<ref name="SCI">{{cite web|title=Andrew Liveris awarded Chemical Industry Medal|url=http://www.soci.org/News/Awards/CIM/Awards-CIM-Liveris|website=Society of Chemical Industry (SCI)|date=1 March 2013|access-date=30 March 2017}}</ref><ref name="ASI2006"/>

Liveris joined Dow's board of directors in February 2004 and became the CEO in November 2004.<ref name="Yale2011"/> Liveris, appointed CEO in 2004 after the board of directors unanimously selected him in part based upon his plan to transform Dow, began to implement the new strategy.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.icis.com/Articles/2008/12/15/9178915/dow-chemical-ceo-andrew-liveris-looks-to-win-in-specialties-and-commodity-jvs-in-spite-of-economic-t.html|title=Dow Chemical CEO Andrew Liveris looks to win in specialties and commodity JVs in spite of economic turmoil}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= http://investing.businessweek.com/research/stocks/people/person.asp?personId=8307189&ticker=DOW:US |archive-url= https://archive.today/20130118201832/http://investing.businessweek.com/research/stocks/people/person.asp?personId=8307189&ticker=DOW:US |url-status= dead |archive-date= 18 January 2013 |title=Andrew Liveris: Executive Profile & Biography – Businessweek |work=investing.businessweek.com|access-date=19 July 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.dow.com/investors/earnings/|title=Dow's Most Recent Earnings Material}}</ref>

His election to [[chairman of the board]] became effective on 1 April 2006.<ref name="Dow2005">{{cite web|title=William Stavropoulos to Retire as Chairman of Dow; Andrew Liveris Elected Chairman Effective April 1, 2006|url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/29915/000002991505000076/exhibit.htm|website=The Dow Chemical Company|access-date=13 December 2005}}</ref> His predecessor was [[William S. Stavropoulos]].

===Rohm and Haas acquisition===
Liveris' strongest move to implement the strategy came with the purchase of [[Rohm and Haas]] in the summer of 2008 for $16.2 billion. This Fortune 500 company, a leader in [[speciality chemicals|specialty chemicals]], was the subject of a global auction, which Dow won with a bid of $16.2 billion. The acquisition proved to be synergistic in terms of growth, allowing a broader and deeper presentation to clients with regard to value-added chemicals, plastics, and materials, but also in terms of costs.<ref name=Wall>{{cite news|url=https://blogs.wsj.com/deals/2009/01/07/parsing-dow-chemical-ceo-andrew-liveris/|title=Parsing Dow Chemical CEO Andrew Liveris | work=The Wall Street Journal | first=Heidi N. | last=Moore | date=7 January 2009}}</ref>

The acquisition closed during the [[2008 financial crisis]]. The credit crisis caused one of Dow's joint venture partners, Petrochemical Industries Company (PIC) of the State of Kuwait, a wholly owned subsidiary of Kuwait Petroleum Corporation (KPC), to withdraw from a planned partnership in basic plastics, despite an agreed contract, depriving Dow of $9 billion in proceeds designated to fund the Rohm and Haas deal. The London-based International Court of Arbitration ruled in March 2012 to award Dow $2.16 Billion plus costs and interest from Kuwait due to its cancellation of the 2008 agreement.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.businessweek.com/news/2012-05-24/dow-awarded-2-dot-16-billion-from-kuwait-over-aborted-deal|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120525124513/http://www.businessweek.com/news/2012-05-24/dow-awarded-2-dot-16-billion-from-kuwait-over-aborted-deal|url-status=dead|archive-date=25 May 2012|title=Dow Awarded $2.16 Billion From Kuwait Over Aborted Deal}}</ref>

In March 2009, Liveris and his management team organised a plan to implement the Rohm and Haas integration, focusing on growth and cost synergies, but also reducing costly debt from the transaction through public offerings, along with equity offers. The plan also called for the divestiture of non-strategic assets, which was accomplished through a sales process that assured maximum valuation.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ameinfo.com/202673.html|title=Dow integration process with Rohm and Haas continues in Middle East}}</ref>

===Later time as CEO===
In 2015, auditors at Dow challenged what they said was improper spending by Liveris. Auditors testified that he used the company's Customer Events Department for personal events including family events and various services. The Liveris family subsequently repaid several hundred thousand dollars to Dow. The head of the auditing department retracted the annual auditing reports for multiple years due to concerns about inaccurate reporting to [[United States Securities and Exchange Commission|the SEC]] and shareholders.<ref name=Schneyer>{{cite news|last1=Schneyer|first1=Joshua|last2=Grow|first2=Brian|title=Dow Chemical's Australian CEO Andrew Liveris challenged on spending for years, documents show|url=http://www.smh.com.au/business/dow-chemicals-australian-ceo-andrew-liveris-challenged-on-spending-for-years-documents-show-20150507-ggvvir.html|access-date=19 October 2015|work=The Sidney Morning Herald|date=7 May 2015}}</ref>

In March 2017, he said the ban on onshore gas exploration by the Victorian Government in Australia was "nonsense," and that he offered "Dow’s unfettered help with no intended positives for Dow" in learning extraction techniques.<ref name="gannon">{{cite news|last1=Gannon |first1=Ed |title=Victorian gas ban 'nonsense', President Trump adviser Andrew Liveris says |url=http://www.weeklytimesnow.com.au/news/national/victorian-gas-ban-nonsense-president-trump-adviser-andrew-liveris-says/news-story/3e6ef13b0e5a8593360302d5ad9aade9 |publisher= Weekly Times Now|date=22 March 2017 }}</ref>

In April 2017, Dow said that it was considering retaining Liveris beyond his planned retirement on 30 June 2017, to help oversee the planned merger between Dow and [[DuPont]].<ref name="kaskj">{{cite news|last1=Kaskey |first1=Jack |title=Dow CEO Liveris May Delay Retirement to Complete DuPont Merger |url=https://www.bloombergquint.com/business/2017/04/27/dow-chemical-boosts-plastics-sales-ahead-of-merger-and-split |publisher=Bloomberg |date=27 April 2017 }}</ref> In May, Dow said that Liveris would retire from the DowDuPont company in mid-2018, serving as executive chairman until between April and July 2018.<ref name="retire">{{cite news|title=Andrew Liveris to retire from combined DowDuPont company mid-2018 |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-dow-liveris-idUSKBN187278 |publisher=Reuters |date= 11 May 2017}}</ref> He stepped down from his executive positions at DowDuPont on 1 April 2018, remaining a director.<ref name="USA-Today">{{Cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/business/2018/03/12/longtime-dow-chemical-chief-andrew-liveris-stepping-down/415810002/|title = Longtime Dow Chemical chief Andrew Liveris is stepping down from management at DowDuPont|website = [[USA Today]]}}</ref> He remained chairman and CEO of The Dow Chemical Company.<ref name="Biography-Dow">{{Cite web|url=https://www.dow.com/en-us/about-dow/our-company/leadership/andrew-n-liveris|title=Former Chairman & CEO Andrew Liveris}}</ref> After his retirement, Liveris outlined plans to author several books and remain tangentially active with Dow. He also said he would join the board of Saudi Aramco.<ref name=Mid /> He toured Dow facilities in 12 countries in June 2018 and was also at the opening of the Andrew N. Liveris Visitors and Heritage Center in Midland.<ref name=Mid />

===Manufacturing council===
In December 2016, Liveris was named by [[Donald Trump]] to lead his [[American Manufacturing Council]].<ref name="Bender">{{cite news|last1=Bender|first1=Michael C.|title=Trump Names Dow Chemical CEO Andrew Liveris to Lead Manufacturing Council|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/trump-names-dow-chemical-ceo-andrew-liveris-to-lead-manufacturing-council-1481340566?mg=id-wsj|access-date=30 March 2017|work=The Wall Street Journal|date=10 December 2016}}</ref><ref name="ABC2016">{{cite news|title=Donald Trump appoints Dow Chemical chief Andrew Liveris as head of manufacturing|url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2016-12-10/trump-appoints-dow-chemical-chief-liveris-to-run-manufacturing/8109334|access-date=30 March 2017|work=ABC News|date=10 December 2016}}</ref> Liveris said Trump created a climate that is conducive to business effectiveness for his company.<ref name="ddiaz">{{cite news|last1=Diaz|first1=Daniella|title=Trump announces Dow Chemical CEO as head of America Manufacturing Council|url=http://www.cnn.com/2016/12/09/politics/andrew-liveris-dow-chemical-ceo-america-manufacturing-council/|access-date=15 May 2017|publisher=CNN|date=9 December 2016}}</ref> On 27 January 2017, Trump publicly announced the names of the 28 members to make up the council,<ref name="Etherington">{{cite news|last1=Etherington|first1=Darrell|title=Trump's manufacturing council includes Elon Musk, Michael Dell and Mark Fields|url=https://techcrunch.com/2017/01/27/trumps-manufacturing-council-includes-elon-musk-michael-dell-and-mark-fields/|access-date=30 March 2017|work=TechCrunch|date=27 January 2017}}</ref> with Liveris heading the Manufacturing Jobs Initiative.<ref name="amptwo">{{cite news|title=Dow's Apprenticeship Program Gets Department of Labor Approval |url=http://www.industryweek.com/workforce/dow-s-apprenticeship-program-gets-department-labor-approval |publisher=Industry Week |date=8 May 2017 }}</ref>

While Liveris was chairman and CEO of Dow Chemical, the company donated $1 million to Trump's presidential inauguration.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://apnews.com/a29073ecef9b4841b2e6cca07202bb67|title=AP Exclusive: Pesticide maker tries to kill risk study|last=Biesecker|first=Michael|date=20 April 2017|website=AP NEWS|access-date=21 May 2019}}</ref> In 2017, the Associated Press reported that Dow was pressuring the Trump administration to ignore risk assessment studies about the harms of pesticides.<ref name=":0" />

===Brisbane 2032 Olympic Organising Committee===
In 2022, Liveris was chosen to lead the organizing committee for the [[2032 Summer Olympics]] and Paralympic Games in [[Brisbane]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1121694/andrew-liveris-brisbane-2032|title = Ex-Dow chief executive Liveris appointed Brisbane 2032 President| date=10 April 2022 | website=Inside The Games  }}</ref>

==Writing==
Liveris is the author of ''Make it in America: The Case for Re-Inventing the Economy'' (first published in 2011, updated in 2012).<ref name="Wiley">{{cite book|last1=Liveris|first1=Andrew|title=Make it in America : the case for re-inventing the economy|date=2012|publisher=Wiley|location=Hoboken, N.J.|isbn=978-1118199626|edition=Updated}}</ref> Liveris argues that a healthy manufacturing sector is essential to creating jobs. Failing to support American manufacturing, as well as research and development, undermines America's potential to engage in new growth sectors such as [[clean energy]] and [[nanotechnology]].<ref name="Schneiderman">{{cite news|last1=Schneiderman|first1=R.M.|title=A CEO's Defense of Government|url=http://www.thedailybeast.com/articles/2011/06/20/andrew-liveris-the-dow-chemical-ceo-defends-government-impresses-clinton.html|access-date=30 March 2017|work=The Daily Beast|date=20 June 2011}}</ref><ref name="Assembled Elsewhere">{{cite news| url = https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052748703398504576100301867568600| title = Assembled Elsewhere| newspaper = Wall Street Journal| date = 25 January 2011| last1 = Hagerty| first1 = James R.}}</ref>

==Memberships==
Liveris has served  on the board of directors of the battery company Novonix,<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.couriermail.com.au/business/dow-chemical-boss-andrew-liveris-plans-to-join-the-board-of-battery-firm-novonix/news-story/d058a6c538403af170d55e6db8bd0042?nk=5c75ef8f3ac5497ba1d6edc67a96bf53-1507134521| title = Reference at www.couriermail.com.au}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.theaustralian.com.au/business/companies/andrew-liveris-to-join-board-of-asxlisted-battery-tech-firm-novonix/news-story/ec024a37fc630fe2a2b120781c933e1f| url-access = subscription| title = Reference at www.theaustralian.com.au}}</ref>  [[IBM]], [[Saudi Aramco]], Worley, [[Lucid Motors]] (chairman as of 2021<ref>{{cite web |title=Board of Directors |url=https://www.lucidmotors.com/company/board/ |website=[[Lucid Motors]] |access-date=27 January 2021}}</ref>).

He is{{when|date=January 2026}} on the advisory board of [[Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation]], Teneo (a global CEO consulting and advisory firm), and NEOM (an initiative driven by Saudi Vision 2030). He is Chairman of the [[BlackRock]] Long Term Capital and a special advisor to the Public Investment Fund (PIF) and the Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia.<ref>[https://liveris-academy.uq.edu.au/andrew-n-liveris-ao]</ref> and a member of the executive committee of the [[Business Roundtable]]. Liveris is also a former president of the [[International Council of Chemical Associations]].<ref name="Pieper">{{cite news|last1=Pieper|first1=James|last2=Heumann|first2=Jenny|title=BASF's Kurt Bock to Lead Global Chemical Industry Association; Dow's Andrew Liveris Completes Successful Two-Year Presidency|url=http://www.americanchemistry.com/Media/PressReleasesTranscripts/ACC-news-releases/BASFs-Kurt-Bock-to-Lead-Global-Chemical-Industry-Association-Dows-Andrew-Liveris-Completes-Succes.html|access-date=30 March 2017|work=American Chemistry Council|date=28 September 2012}}</ref>

He served as vice-chairman of [[The Business Council]] for 2011 and 2012, and as chairman for 2013 and 2014.<ref name="committee">{{cite web| url = http://www.thebusinesscouncil.org/about/excommittee.aspx| title = The Business Council, Official website, Executive Committee| access-date = 10 January 2017| archive-date = 21 July 2013| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130721074619/http://www.thebusinesscouncil.org/about/excommittee.aspx| url-status = dead}}</ref><ref name="dow">{{Cite web |url=http://www.dow.com/news/all-news/article/?id=%2Fcompany-news%2Fdow-chairman-and-ceo-andrew-liveris-elected-chairman%C2%A0-business-council |title=Dow Chairman and CEO Andrew Liveris Elected Chairman, The Business Council dow.com, 19 October 2012 |access-date=18 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121022233221/http://www.dow.com/news/all-news/article/?id=%2Fcompany-news%2Fdow-chairman-and-ceo-andrew-liveris-elected-chairman%C2%A0-business-council |archive-date=22 October 2012 |url-status=dead  }}</ref><ref name="yahoo">Press Release: The Dow Chemical Company, {{cite web| url = https://finance.yahoo.com/news/dow-chairman-ceo-andrew-liveris-174000939.html| title = Dow Chairman and CEO Andrew Liveris Elected Chairman, The Business Council}}, ''[[Yahoo!]]'', 19 October 2012</ref><ref name="wsgw">{{cite web| url = http://www.wsgw.com/common/more.php?m=15&r=1&item_id=4221| title = Dow Chief To Head National Business Organization| access-date = 10 January 2017| archive-date = 19 December 2013| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20131219075126/http://www.wsgw.com/common/more.php?m=15&r=1&item_id=4221| url-status = dead}} ''[[WSGW (AM)|WSGW]]''</ref> He is a member of the [[Peterson Institute for International Economics]], and the [[American Australian Association]].<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.americanaustralian.org/| title = American Australian Association}}</ref>

Liveris is{{when|date=January 2026}} on the board of trustees for the [[United States Council for International Business]] and is a trustee of the [[California Institute of Technology]]. Liveris is a member of the Business Advisory Board for the [[University of Technology Sydney]] (UTS) Business School. In April 2012 he became a member of the Special Olympics International board of directors.<ref>{{cite web|title=Special Olympics Announces Additions to International Board of Directors|url=http://www.specialolympics.org/Press/2012/April_2012_Board_of_Directors_Meeting.aspx|website=Special Olympics|access-date=30 March 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url = http://datasearch.uts.edu.au/business/news-events/news-detail.cfm?ItemId=30326| title = Business Advisory Board for the University of Technology Sydney (UTS) Business School}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.specialolympics.org/Press/2012/April_2012_Board_of_Directors_Meeting.aspx| title = Special Olympics Announces Additions to International board of directors}}</ref>

Liveris collaborated with [[Muhtar Kent]], chairman and CEO of The Coca-Cola Company, [[George David]], chairman of the Coca-Cola Hellenic Bottling Company, and George Stamas, partner at Kirkland and Ellis LLP, to found The Hellenic Initiative (THI), a non-profit, non-governmental organization to encourage entrepreneurship and job-creation investments in Greece.<ref name="Papapostolou">{{cite news|last1=Papapostolou|first1=Anastasios|title=The Hellenic Initiative Announces 3rd Annual Banquet|url=http://usa.greekreporter.com/2015/08/28/the-hellenic-initiative-announces-3rd-annual-banquet/|access-date=30 March 2017|work=Greek Reporter|date=28 August 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenationalherald.com/207037/this-venture-fair-spotlights-greeces-young-entrepreneurs/|title = THI's Venture Fair Spotlights Greece's Young Entrepreneurs}}</ref>

The $250 billion Saudi Arabia [[Public Investment Fund]] (PIF) appointed Andrew Liveris as a special adviser on matters of strategic importance, to assist the fund in efforts to boost the value of its portfolio and ensure the contribution of PIF companies to [[Saudi Arabia]]'s economic vision program 2030.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2018/09/02/business/saudi-sovereign-fund-appoints-former-dow-chemical-ceo-andrew-liveris-special-adviser/#.W5ufIy2fnOQ|title = Saudi sovereign fund appoints former Dow Chemical CEO Andrew Liveris as special adviser|date = 2 September 2018}}</ref> He has also joined the board of Australia's WorleyParsons.<ref>{{cite web| url = ==Awards and recognition==
* 2005: [[Honorary doctorate]] in science from University of Queensland; also Alumnus of the Year<ref name="ASI2006">{{cite news|title=Applause: Liveris Receives Honorary Doctorate from University of Queensland; Named Alumnus of the Year|url=http://www.adhesivesmag.com/articles/86594-applause-liveris-receives-honorary-doctorate-from-university-of-queensland-named-alumnus-of-the-year|access-date=30 March 2017|work=ASI: Adhesives & Sealants|date=27 February 2006}}</ref>
* 2010, 2012, and 2013: named No. 1 Power Player in the global chemical markets by ICIS Chemical Business magazine<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.dow.com/news/corporate/2010/20101213a.htm |title=Andrew Liveris of Dow Chemical Ranked No. 1 on ICIS Top 40 Power Players |access-date=7 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111203045413/http://www.dow.com/news/corporate/2010/20101213a.htm |archive-date=3 December 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.icis.com/Articles/2012/12/10/9622048/corrected-icis-top-40-power-players-dow-ceo-andrew-liveris-takes-top-spot-for-2012.html| title = ICIS Top 40 Power Players: Dow CEO Andrew Liveris takes top spot for 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release| url = http://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/icis-top-40-power-players-ranking-for-2013-revealed-235994731.html| title = ICIS Top 40 Power Players Ranking for 2013 Revealed}}</ref>
* 2011: [[George E. Davis Medal]], [[Institution of Chemical Engineers]] (IChemE).<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.icheme.org/media_centre/news/2013/liveris%20to%20give%20davis%20lecture.aspx#.UVvYWKKzeSo |title=Liveris to give Davis Lecture |access-date=3 April 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170113025916/http://www.icheme.org/media_centre/news/2013/liveris%20to%20give%20davis%20lecture.aspx#.UVvYWKKzeSo |archive-date=13 January 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* 2011: Distinguished Performance Award for Excellence in Public Policy from the [[Committee for Economic Development]]<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.ced.org/annual-dinner/2011-annual-dinner/distinquished-performance-awards-dinnerInternational| title = Leadership Award Presented to Andrew Liveris}}</ref>
* 2011: International Leadership Award from the [[United States Council for International Business]] (USCIB)<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.dow.com/about/insights/multimedia/20111116a.htm| title = 2011 Distinguished Performance Awards Dinner}}</ref>
* 2011: Legend in Leadership from the Yale Chief Executive Leadership Institute at the [[Yale School of Management]]<ref name="Yale2011">{{cite web|title=Yale Chief Executive Leadership Institute to Honor The Dow Chemical Company Chairman and CEO Andrew Liveris with Yale Legend in Leadership Award|url=http://som.yale.edu/news/news/yale-chief-executive-leadership-institute-honor-dow-chemical-company-chairman-and-ceo|access-date=30 March 2017|website=Yale School of Management|date=15 December 2011}}</ref>
* 2011: CEO of the year, Platts Global Energy Awards<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.platts.com/PressReleases/2011/120111| title = Brazil's Petrobras wins "Company" and "Producer of the Year" Honors at Platts Global Energy Awards as "CEO" Goes to Dow Chemical's Liveris}}</ref>
* February 2012: Archbishop Iakovos Leadership 100 Award for Excellence<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.l100.org/Default.aspx?tabid=333| title = Leadership 100}}</ref>
* March 2012: Aristeio Award in Business from the American Hellenic Council<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.americanhellenic.org/press/2012-04-06_ahc_awards_gala_pr.php |title=The American Hellenic Council honored Andrew Liveris, Rep. Shelley Berkley and Phedon Papamichael in 2012 Annual Awards Gala on 31 March in Los Angeles |access-date=24 April 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120413235900/http://www.americanhellenic.org/press/2012-04-06_ahc_awards_gala_pr.php |archive-date=13 April 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* March 2012: Foreign co-chair at the [[China Development Forum]] in Beijing, representing more than 200 overseas delegates including the leaders of more than 70 Fortune 500 companies, international organisations, senior officials and internationally renowned scholars<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cdrf.org.cn/plus/list.php?tid=73 |title=China Development Forum |access-date=21 March 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140903071706/http://www.cdrf.org.cn/plus/list.php?tid=73 |archive-date=3 September 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.dow.com/news/corporate/2012/20120318a.htm |title=Liveris Presides over China Development Forum as 2012 Co-Chair, Delivers Opening Remarks |access-date=21 March 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120625001306/http://www.dow.com/news/corporate/2012/20120318a.htm |archive-date=25 June 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* August 2012: Named by ''[[The Australian Financial Review]]'' to the BOSS list of True Leaders.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.afr.com/p/boss/true_leaders_asia_and_beyond_pp1kXGNlmr0fdZwV8RIKoL| title = True Leaders {{!}} Asia and beyond}}</ref>
* 2013: [[International Palladium Medal]] of the Société de Chimie Industrielle (announced in 2012)<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.dow.com/news/all-news/article/?id=%2Fcompany-news%2Fandrew-liveris-chairman-and-ceo-dow-chemical-company-be-awarded-2013-inte |title=Andrew Liveris, Chairman and CEO of The Dow Chemical Company, to be Awarded the 2013 International Palladium Medal |access-date=28 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121006010519/http://www.dow.com/news/all-news/article/?id=%2Fcompany-news%2Fandrew-liveris-chairman-and-ceo-dow-chemical-company-be-awarded-2013-inte |archive-date=6 October 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* March 2013: [[Chemical Industry Medal]] from the [[Society of Chemical Industry]] (SCI)<ref name="SCI"/>
* May 2013: Eisenhower Award by [[Business Executives for National Security]] (BENS) at a ceremony in Washington, D.C.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.bens.org/document.doc?id=211| title = BENS to Honor Gen. Raymond T. Odierno, USA and Andrew N. Liveris, Chairman, President & CEO, Dow Chemical with Eisenhower Award}}</ref>
* January 2014: Appointed [[Officer of the Order of Australia]] (AO) in the [[2014 Australia Day Honours]], "for distinguished service to international business through senior roles with multinational organisations, as a supporter of Australia-US educational and cultural relations, and to the community."<ref>{{cite web|title=Officer (AO) in the General Division of the Order of Australia|url=http://www.gg.gov.au/sites/default/files/files/honours/ad/Media%20Notes%20-%20AO%20(final).pdf|work=Website of the Governor General of Australia|publisher=Australian Honours and Awards Secretariat|access-date=18 September 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140127075149/http://www.gg.gov.au/sites/default/files/files/honours/ad/Media%20Notes%20-%20AO%20(final).pdf|archive-date=27 January 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.theaustralian.com.au/in-depth/australia-day/dows-andrew-liveris-awarded-ao-for-services-to-international-business/story-fnl4gv3e-1226810340056| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160303235524/http://www.theaustralian.com.au/in-depth/australia-day/dows-andrew-liveris-awarded-ao-for-services-to-international-business/story-fnl4gv3e-1226810340056| url-status = dead| archive-date = 3 March 2016| title = Dow's Andrew Liveris awarded AO for services to international business.}} ''The Australian'' {{subscription required}}</ref>
